summary: The last reachable next pointer can distinguish an acyclic n-node chain from a cycle whose entry is the head, so locating the entry requires Omega(n) work in the worst case. Floyd's two phases match that bound with constant space.

optimality.argument: Consider an n-node chain whose final next field is either null or points to the head. The two inputs agree along every earlier edge but require answers null and head, respectively. A correct algorithm must therefore reach and inspect the final node in the worst case, taking Omega(n) traversals. Floyd's detection and entry-location phases, plus the app adapter's position count, each perform at most linear work, giving O(n) total time.

replacement_checks.evidence: Changing only the final reachable next field from null to the head changes both cycle existence and the required entry result.
Detection, equal-speed convergence to the entry, and app-local position serialization each traverse at most a constant multiple of the reachable nodes.

The source-fidelity-verified examples cover an entry after a prefix, an entry at the head, and no cycle; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
